title: Types you write down
objectives: annotate a variable with a type
say why any is a last resort

steps.instruction: You can write the type yourself. Put it after a colon.
body: TypeScript already worked this out from 15.
Writing it down says what you meant, so a wrong value is caught at the line you wrote it.
string for text. number for any number, whole or decimal. boolean for true and false.
All lowercase. String with a capital S is a different thing and not what you want.

steps.instruction: Declare three variables with types written out: a string, a number, a boolean. Print all three.
steps.after: The colon says what goes in. The value has to match.
You said number. Text is not a number.

body: There is one number type. It holds whole numbers and decimals alike.
So you never have to pick between them.
steps.keypoint: number covers whole numbers and decimals.

steps.why: "true" in quotes is text. A boolean is true or false with no quotes.
skills: tell a boolean from the text true

steps.instruction: You do not always have to write it.
body: TypeScript reads the value and decides.
Most code leaves the type off when the value makes it obvious.
steps.keypoint: Write the type when it is not obvious. Otherwise let TypeScript read it.

steps.hint: Look at each value. Quotes, digits, or true and false.
steps.after: The value tells you the type.

steps.instruction: A function is a piece of code with a name.
body: double(5) runs the code inside with x set to 5.
return is the value that comes back out.
Write it once, use it as often as you like.

steps.instruction: Write a function called double that takes x and returns x times 2. Do not write any types.
steps.after: TypeScript cannot tell what x is, so it refuses to guess.

steps.instruction: Fix it. Tell TypeScript that x is a number, then print double(21).
steps.after: Now it knows what goes in, so it knows what comes out.

body: any accepts everything and reports nothing.
It is a way to silence TypeScript, which is the opposite of why you are using it.
Use it when you genuinely do not know yet. Not to make an error go away.
steps.keypoint: any turns off type checking. Reach for it last.

steps.instruction: Write a function greet that takes a name of type string and returns "Hi, " followed by the name. Print greet("Ada").
steps.after: A typed parameter, a value back, and no warnings.
